finding.claim: SQL injection in list_users_sorted: $_GET['sort'] is concatenated unvalidated into an ORDER BY clause and executed via PDO::query, allowing arbitrary SQL expressions (e.g. scalar subqueries/CASE) to read any table through ordering or error side-channels.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) (list.php:6)

trace.note: concatenated into SQL text for ORDER BY

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, cast, or quoting on $sort; ?? only defaults null; query() with concatenated string does not bind parameters. list_users_safe (lines 9-13) has an allowlist but is not called from list_users_sorted. find_user (15-19) uses a bound parameter and is not affected. No auth check visible in this file; reachability from an unauthenticated request depends on callers outside this directory. PDO sqlite likely executes only the first statement, limiting stacked writes (unverified).

verdict.guard_found: none in list_users_sorted (list.php:4-7): $_GET['sort'] is concatenated into the ORDER BY string with no allowlist, cast, or binding. list_users_safe (list.php:9-13) has an allowlist but is not called by list_users_sorted. find_user (list.php:15-19) uses a bound parameter and is unrelated.
verdict.reason: The source and sink lines (list.php:5-6) match the claim, but list.php never calls list_users_sorted: the file only defines functions (list.php:4-19) and the top-level code at list.php:2 just opens the PDO connection, so the trace's "executed" step never happens here. The only way to reach the sink is a caller outside this directory, and none exists in the provided code, so the attacker's reachability cannot be decided from it. The unsafe concatenation is real as a latent flaw, but the finding as written (an unauthenticated request reaching it) is unverified.
